standard_prerequisites: Chapter basics: a splitting field of a separable polynomial is a normal separable (Galois) extension; x^p - 1 is separable over K when p differs from char(K) (derivative p x^{p-1} is nonzero)
Same chapter: lemma-finite-Galois (a finite Galois group has order equal to the degree); a K-automorphism of K(zeta) is determined by the image of the generator zeta
core_obligations: x^p - 1 splits completely over K(zeta) with roots 1, zeta, ..., zeta^{p-1}, so K(zeta)/K is a splitting field and hence normal
x^p - 1 is a separable polynomial, so the extension is separable; normal + separable = Galois
Any K-automorphism sends zeta to another root zeta^i with 1 <= i <= p-1 (the image preserves the order-p element), so Gal(K(zeta)/K) is a subgroup of (Z/pZ)^*
proof_roadmap: Splitting field argument gives normality, separability of the polynomial gives separability
Bound the Galois group inside (Z/pZ)^* by tracking where zeta can go
